input.prompt:
You review a set of behaviour specifications that will each be implemented, one after the other, on the same domain classes. Find specifications that cannot all be true together.

## Product intent
- Product type: game
- Audience: casual players
- Goal: Let a player clear a grid of hidden cells without detonating any mines, using numeric clues about adjacent mines.
- Scope: A single-player minesweeper game consisting of a mine grid, cell reveal and flag interactions, win/loss detection, and basic scoring such as elapsed time.
- The model must cover: game board with grid dimensions, mine placement and per-cell state (hidden, revealed, flagged); adjacent mine counts and cascade reveal of empty regions; game session lifecycle including start, win and loss conditions; difficulty settings controlling grid size and mine count; scoring via elapsed time and remaining flag counter
- Do NOT model: user accounts and authentication; multiplayer or online matchmaking; monetization, in-app purchases or advertising; administrative back-office or content management

## Specifications
- SPEC-001 [Rectangular grid with fixed mine count] (Game): Given a game configured with width W, height H and mine count M When the mines are laid Then the board has exactly W×H cells and exactly M cells hold a mine
- SPEC-002 [Beginner preset] (Game): Given the player chooses Beginner When the new game is created Then its width is 9, height is 9 and mine count is 10
- SPEC-003 [Intermediate preset] (Game): Given the player chooses Intermediate When the new game is created Then its width is 16, height is 16 and mine count is 40
- SPEC-004 [Expert preset] (Game): Given the player chooses Expert When the new game is created Then its width is 30, height is 16 and mine count is 99
- SPEC-005 [Custom width range] (Game): Given the player enters a Custom configuration When the width is between 9 and 30 inclusive Then the width is accepted, and When the width is below 9 or above 30 Then the configuration is refused
- SPEC-006 [Custom height range] (Game): Given the player enters a Custom configuration When the height is between 9 and 24 inclusive Then the height is accepted, and When the height is below 9 or above 24 Then the configuration is refused
- SPEC-007 [Custom mine count range] (Game): Given a Custom configuration with valid width W and height H When the mine count is between 10 and (W−1)×(H−1) inclusive Then it is accepted, and When it is below 10 or above (W−1)×(H−1) Then the configuration is refused
- SPEC-008 [Invalid custom leaves current game unchanged] (Game): Given a game in any status When the player submits a Custom configuration outside the limits Then a validation message is shown and the current game, its board, timer and counter remain unchanged
- SPEC-009 [Custom validation message display] (Game): Given the Custom difficulty dialog When the player submits out-of-range values Then a message explaining the allowed limits is displayed
- SPEC-010 [Mines laid on first open] (Game): Given a game in Ready status with no mines laid When the player opens the first cell Then the mines are laid at that moment, and before that moment no cell holds a mine
- SPEC-011 [First click is safe] (Game): Given a game in Ready status When the player opens any cell as the first open Then that cell holds no mine and the game does not end in a loss
- SPEC-012 [Ready to Playing transition] (Game): Given a game in Ready status When the player opens a hidden unflagged cell Then the game status becomes Playing
- SPEC-013 [Open a hidden unflagged cell] (Game): Given a game in Ready or Playing status and a cell in Hidden state When the player opens it Then the cell state becomes Opened (or Detonated if it holds a mine)
- SPEC-014 [Neighbour mine count] (Game): Given an interior safe cell with K mines among its 8 neighbours When it is opened Then its adjacent mine count is K (0 to 8)
- SPEC-015 [Edge and corner neighbours] (Game): Given a safe cell on an edge (5 neighbours) or a corner (3 neighbours) When its adjacent mine count is computed Then only the neighbours that exist within the grid are counted
- SPEC-016 [Cascade on zero] (Game): Given a hidden safe cell with adjacent mine count 0 When it is opened Then all its hidden neighbours are opened, and any opened neighbour with count 0 opens its neighbours in turn
- SPEC-017 [Cascade stops at numbered cells] (Game): Given a cascade in progress When it opens a cell with adjacent mine count of 1 or more Then that cell is opened and its own neighbours are not opened by the cascade
- SPEC-018 [Cascade skips flagged cells] (Game): Given a cascade in progress and a neighbouring cell in Flagged state When the cascade reaches it Then the cell remains Flagged and is not opened
- SPEC-019 [Toggle flag] (Game): Given a game in Ready or Playing status When the player flags a Hidden cell Then it becomes Flagged, and When the player flags a Flagged cell Then it becomes Hidden
- SPEC-020 [Flagged cell cannot be opened] (Game): Given a cell in Flagged state When the player tries to open it Then the cell stays Flagged and nothing is revealed, and When the player unflags it and opens it Then it is opened
- SPEC-021 [Unlimited flags] (Game): Given a game whose flags placed already equals its mine count When the player flags another Hidden cell Then the flag is placed
- SPEC-022 [Remaining mines counter] (Game): Given a game with M mines and F flags placed When the counter is calculated Then it equals M − F, including negative values when F > M
- SPEC-023 [Chord with matching flags] (Game): Given a game in Playing status and an Opened cell with number N and exactly N flagged neighbours When the player chords it Then all its Hidden unflagged neighbours are opened (with cascades as applicable)
- SPEC-024 [Chord with mismatched flags does nothing] (Game): Given an Opened cell with number N and a number of flagged neighbours different from N When the player chords it Then no cell changes state
- SPEC-025 [Chord with wrong flag loses] (Game): Given an Opened cell with number N and N flagged neighbours, one of which is not a mine When the player chords it Then the unflagged mine neighbour is opened, becomes Detonated and the game status becomes Lost
- SPEC-026 [Timer starts at first open] (Game): Given a game in Ready status with elapsed seconds 0 When the player opens the first cell Then the timer starts and elapsed seconds increases by 1 each second
- SPEC-027 [Timer cap at 999] (Game): Given a game in Playing status with elapsed seconds 999 When further time passes Then elapsed seconds stays at 999
- SPEC-028 [Timer freezes on end] (Game): Given a game in Playing status When the game becomes Won or Lost Then elapsed seconds is frozen at its current value
- SPEC-029 [Opening a mine loses] (Game): Given a game in Playing status When the player opens a Hidden cell holding a mine Then the cell becomes Detonated, it is recorded as the struck cell and the game status becomes Lost
- SPEC-030 [Loss display] (Game): Given a game that has just become Lost When the board is displayed Then the struck mine is drawn on a red background, every other mine is revealed, and each flag on a non-mine cell is drawn as a crossed-out mine
- SPEC-031 [Win condition] (Game): Given a game in Playing status When the last non-mine cell is opened Then the game status becomes Won whether or not the mines are flagged, and while any non-mine cell is unopened the game is not Won
- SPEC-032 [Auto-flag on win] (Game): Given a game that has just become Won When the win is recorded Then every mine cell is set to Flagged, flags placed equals the mine count and the remaining-mines counter is 0
- SPEC-033 [Win display] (Game): Given a game that is Won When the board is displayed Then every mine shows a red pennant flag and the mine counter displays 0
- SPEC-034 [New best time] (BestTime): Given a stored best time of B seconds for a standard difficulty When the player wins a game of that difficulty in T seconds with T < B Then the best time becomes T for that difficulty on this device
- SPEC-035 [First win sets best time] (BestTime): Given no best time stored for a standard difficulty When the player wins a game of that difficulty in T seconds Then a best time of T is recorded for that difficulty
- SPEC-036 [Slower or equal win keeps best] (BestTime): Given a stored best time of B seconds for a standard difficulty When the player wins in T seconds with T >= B Then the best time remains B
- SPEC-037 [Custom games record no best time] (BestTime): Given a game on Custom difficulty When the player wins it Then no best time is created or changed
- SPEC-038 [Lost or abandoned games record no best time] (BestTime): Given a game that ends Lost or Abandoned When it ends Then no best time is created or changed
- SPEC-039 [Board lock after end] (Game): Given a game in Won or Lost status When the player opens, flags or chords any cell Then no cell, counter or timer changes, and When the player starts a new game Then it is accepted
- SPEC-040 [Opening an opened cell is ignored] (Game): Given a cell in Opened state When the player opens it Then nothing changes and no message is shown
- SPEC-041 [Flagging an opened cell is ignored] (Game): Given a cell in Opened state When the player toggles a flag on it Then the cell stays Opened, flags placed is unchanged and no message is shown
- SPEC-042 [Chording a hidden cell is ignored] (Game): Given a cell in Hidden state When the player chords it Then no cell changes state and no message is shown
- SPEC-043 [Restart via smiley] (Game): Given a game in Ready or Playing status When the player presses the smiley Then that game becomes Abandoned with no best time recorded and a new Ready game of the same difficulty with all cells Hidden, timer 0 and counter equal to its mine count is created
- SPEC-044 [Smiley after end starts new game] (Game): Given a game in Won or Lost status When the player presses the smiley Then the finished game keeps its outcome and a new Ready game of the same difficulty is created
- SPEC-045 [Changing difficulty] (Game): Given a game in Ready or Playing status When the player chooses a valid difficulty Then the current game becomes Abandoned with no score and a new Ready game with the chosen width, height and mine count is created
- SPEC-046 [Leaving abandons the game] (Game): Given a game in Ready or Playing status When the player closes the game Then it becomes Abandoned and no best time is recorded
- SPEC-047 [Abandon only from Ready or Playing] (Game): Given a game in Ready or Playing status When it is abandoned Then its status becomes Abandoned, and Given a game in Won or Lost status When an abandon is triggered Then its status remains Won or Lost
- SPEC-048 [Game status transitions] (Game): Given a game in any status When a transition is requested Then only Ready→Playing, Playing→Won, Playing→Lost and Ready or Playing→Abandoned are allowed and all other transitions are refused
- SPEC-049 [Cell state transitions] (Game): Given a cell When its state changes Then only Hidden↔Flagged, Hidden→Opened (safe) and Hidden→Detonated (mine) are allowed, and an Opened or Detonated cell never returns to Hidden or Flagged
- SPEC-050 [Classic window frame] (Game): Given the game is displayed When the player views it Then it is shown inside a grey, bevelled, raised window frame
- SPEC-051 [Header mine counter] (Game): Given a game is displayed When the player views the header strip Then the remaining-mines value appears on the left as red digits on black, including a minus sign when negative
- SPEC-052 [Header timer] (Game): Given a game is displayed When the player views the header strip Then elapsed seconds appear on the right as red digits on black
- SPEC-053 [Smiley button placement] (Game): Given a game is displayed When the player views the header strip Then a yellow smiley button is centred between the counter and the timer
- SPEC-054 [Smiley faces] (Game): Given a game is displayed When a cell is being pressed Then the smiley shows a surprised O, When the game is Won Then it wears sunglasses, When the game is Lost Then it shows crossed-out eyes, and otherwise it shows a normal smile
- SPEC-055 [Hidden and opened cell appearance] (Game): Given the board is displayed When a cell is Hidden or Flagged Then it is drawn as a raised grey tile, and When it is Opened Then it is drawn flat in lighter grey with thin grid lines
- SPEC-056 [Number colours] (Game): Given an Opened safe cell with adjacent count N When it is displayed Then N=1 is blue, 2 green, 3 red, 4 navy, 5 maroon, 6 teal, 7 black, 8 grey, and N=0 shows no number
- SPEC-057 [Flag and mine icons] (Game): Given the board is displayed When a cell is Flagged Then it shows a small red pennant, and When a mine is revealed Then it shows a black spiked ball
- SPEC-058 [Open control] (Game): Given a game is displayed When the player left-clicks or taps a cell Then an open action is issued for that cell
- SPEC-059 [Flag control] (Game): Given a game is displayed When the player right-clicks or long-presses a cell Then a flag toggle action is issued for that cell
- SPEC-060 [Chord control] (Game): Given a game is displayed When the player clicks an Opened numbered cell Then a chord action is issued for that cell
- SPEC-061 [Difficulty menu] (Difficulty): Given the game is displayed When the player opens the difficulty menu Then it lists Beginner, Intermediate, Expert and Custom, and choosing Custom asks for width, height and mine count
- SPEC-062 [Best time shown per standard difficulty] (BestTime): Given best times stored on this device When the player views best times Then the fastest win for Beginner, Intermediate and Expert is shown, and Custom has no entry

Report only real contradictions: two or more specifications that demand incompatible results for the same situation (for example one says an inquiry is accepted when a field is missing and another says it is rejected). Do not report overlaps, duplicates, missing detail or style differences.

Respond STRICTLY with JSON, no commentary:
{"conflicts": [{"specs": ["<spec_id>", "<spec_id>"], "reason": "<one sentence naming the incompatible demands>"}]}
Use an empty list when there are none.
